entries.subject: A pact in its last half minute asks whether to renew it; the bar across the top keeps to the places you go, and the rest is found by scrolling
A house can be renamed from inside the lobby while the lords are still gathering
An invitation link takes you straight into the lobby
The landing page has a bar of tabs across the top and one centred column: the name, the public games with the next one large, and the ways to play
Account names: chosen once, apart from the house name, and what a clan's roll goes by. The landing page's tagline loses the box it picked up from the clan tags
Clan tags may be five characters; a clan's roll follows the house name each member plays under
The server's dashboard looks after the clans: reported clans, every clan, and the banned words
Clans: a word filter on names, tags and descriptions, and a link to report a clan
Clans: found or join one, carry its tag before your house name, and see where they gather on a map of the world
The Stats tab is a chronicle in chapters with a seal and a treasury in bars; any signed-in house may fly a plain banner in muted colours
Signing in is its own switch, apart from the store: Discord, Google, Steam or an emailed link. A signed-in player has a record (standing, full statistics by kind of game) and a Customisation tab
The small AI realms are called tribes
While the wheel is open the pointer is a plain arrow everywhere
A click away from the wheel only closes it; a right-click while placing only puts the thing down
The wheel has four coloured slices like a compass: realm above, sea to the right, pacts below, attack or build to the left
The wheel: Build on your own land (town, market, harbour, mage tower, ballista tower), Attack elsewhere (war galley, fireball, dragon, starfall)
The wheel offers building only on your own land
Realm labels carry a dagger for an oathbreaker and a barred coin where trade is stopped; the realm card is laid out in blocks with betrayals, trading and pacts
Right-click opens a wheel: march in the middle, with building, sailing, pacts, gifts and a card on the realm around it
The conquest banner is smaller
The conquest banner fades sooner
The house name is remembered between visits
Conquering a realm is marked on the map: gold rings and a fountain where its last ground fell, and a banner with its name and the gold taken
Graphics levels: high, medium and low, chosen for the device, lowered when the game runs slowly, or set by hand
House rules can be set for a solo game too
Map pictures are painted without WebGL, so the landing page holds one graphics context, not two; a visit that died while drawing the backdrop leaves it off next time and is reported
Fault reports from crawlers and page testers are left out of the server log
The landing page keeps a dark backdrop until the live one is drawing, starts it again if the browser drops the graphics, and reports the loss; no extra graphics context for the acceleration check
While placing, the roads the new building would lay are drawn as dotted lines
While placing, the rings and a marker show where the building will really stand once it has been moved clear of its neighbours
While placing, a building that the click would raise a level is ringed in gold and the hint says so
The landing page no longer carries the line about the realm behind it
The dragon's cursor is three fireballs
While placing, the cursor is a picture of what is being placed
On the real-world maps, kingdoms carry the names of the medieval realms that stood where they start
War galleys hold a steady heading instead of wagging at every tile
Five new maps: Mirrormere, The Serpent, The Four Realms, The Shattered Isles and The Maelstrom
Longship notices show a boat beside the levy count
Longship notices share the attack notices' columns and look the same
Click a pact offer to see the realm that sent it
A single attack or longship notice stays in the left column
House rules for private games: starting gold, income, truce, time limit, pact length, no pacts or gifts, instant building, and bans
The longship cursor shows only where ships would really be sent; a bordering realm gets the sword anywhere on its land
The cursor shows what a click will do; shift-drag a box round war galleys to command them together
Starfall marks where each falling star will land with a red circle
Fireballs and dragons in flight mark where they will land with a red circle; the in-flight line is gone
Flight lines for fireballs and dragons are drawn with many more dots
Clans show their levies under their name on the map; the status bar shows levies gained per turn
Each attack and longship notice is its own box
Attack notices sit two abreast too
Longship notices sit two abreast
A notice when longships are bound for your shores (click it to see the ship); on the Crown Isles nobody starts on the great isle
Pact offers appear at the bottom centre, with the attack notices
A phone layout with touch controls; public games shown as large pictures of their realms
3D previews of the realms in the map picker and beside each public game
A public game nobody joins is swapped for a different realm, so the list turns over every half minute
New map: The Crown Isles, nine large islands in a ring around a greater one
Three public games are open at once, on different realms, starting half a minute apart
Two original maps: The Sundered Sea and Ironspine
A pact shows as linked rings above your ally's label, fading as it runs out and pulsing when it can be renewed
A dropped connection mid-game now reconnects by itself and carries on from the turn it missed
Fix the freeze while placing buildings; the server install now really replaces the maps; a realm taken from the server is drawn as the server has it
Maps rebuilt so sea routes never cross land: no water thinner than four tiles, no hidden ponds
Ships and their wakes are kept off the land: every drawn position is stood off the shore by the ship's beam
The land is flat: hills and mountains are painted on, so nothing sails or marches through a hillside
Map labels, the realm list and tooltips show each house's own designed arms
Store: confirm before spending Crowns; no paying for a house name or bundle you already own
Aiming a fireball or dragon shows its flight and whether a ballista tower covers it; sea trail cards in the store are live 3D
Sea trails are translucent and soft-edged so they sit in the water
Arms editor: choose the colour of your charge
Store: snail knights, geese, swan boats, tower turtles, toadstool towns and more new 3D sets; all 2D items are now medieval heraldry
Longships trace their route with a dotted line; 54 sea trails in the store
Narrow straits show as water, war galleys get health bars, longships leave a wake, sorcery shows its flight line
Signed-in players keep their reserved house name even if the page connected before sign-in
Multiplayer games give 30 seconds to choose a starting spot
Territory runs to the waterline and borders are rounded instead of stepped
No splash when trade ships arrive at a harbour
Building level numbers go past 40 (up to 256)
Store: new troop, ship and building models, 57 territory cloths, bigger arms editor, shop with live 3D previews
Store: Crown packs, cosmetics for territory, banner, ships, buildings and troops, bundles, reserved house names
Answer button is a sword
Troop counts on the front lines, war list above the player strip, Answer button on incoming attacks
Build bar shows how many of each you have; standings move to the top left
HUD: player strip beside the attack slider, chronicle on the right, blast rings, merged rings
Colour every land tile; kingdom and clan counts match upstream
Never draw the waiting room over a running game; browsers must revalidate map files
Fix second game never starting; server log shows each client's start steps
Fix multiplayer desync: keep turns that arrive while the map downloads; bridge narrow rivers and gaps; flatter mountains
Public games: countdown on the server's clock, failed starts reported instead of hanging
Smaller war galleys, much smaller merchant cogs
Remove install transcript from the repo
Changelog and build version generated from git on every deploy
Server dashboard: live view and controls at /admin
Fix Windows service install args
Tell the player when the game server is out of date
Flatter mountains so buildings sit on slopes, not cliffs
Real-world realms (Earth, Europe, Mediterranean, Greece), range rings and building levels
Install script: substitute the right placeholder
Server: default hostname play.crusades.io
renamed to crusades.io
added source URL
initial commit
